acceptance_policy.numeric_claims: Measured, provider-reported, derived, estimated, inferred, and unavailable values must never share the same unqualified label.
acceptance_policy.repo_target: Core logic coverage above 95 percent and zero linter warnings before a release claim.

prd_items.title: Dashboard data truth audit
prd_items.summary: Truth-safety fixes are implemented and all eight tabs were inspected in the installed app. History rendering is collapsed, indexed and batch-limited; the misleading RAM purge action is removed because macOS purge cannot clear inactive pages. The v1.3.1 release candidate packages the origin/main coverage changes and passes the repository coverage gate; destructive-action paths remain deliberately manual.
acceptance_criteria: Every displayed number has a named source and freshness timestamp.
Estimated or inferred values are visibly labeled and excluded from factual totals.
Unavailable measurements never masquerade as facts: analytical grids omit empty fields, while safety-critical controls expose an explicit reason and fail closed.
All eight tabs pass automated and manual checks.

test_cases.fixture: Fan helper active; helper response available over local socket
test_cases.expected: Only physical sensor readings drive safety actions; partial writes and unavailable RPM are reported honestly.
evidence: Root cause reproduced: the shipped AppleSMC payload was 76 bytes instead of the required 80 bytes, and read metadata was discarded before decoding.
Installed helper 1.1.0 returned FNum=2 and both fans' measured RPM and hardware ranges.
A read-only Apple IOHID probe returned named PMU tdie*, NAND CH* temp, and gas-gauge battery temperatures; raw SMC Tp/Tg/Tm keys are no longer attributed to CPU/GPU/RAM.
At 21:45 the installed Fan page showed 14 named PMU samples at 60.7–64.8 C, NAND 36.0 C, AppleSmartBattery 35.7 C, and actual fan readbacks 3170/3436 RPM.

At 23:44 the installed page rendered exactly three measured component groups backed by 16 readings: 14 named PMU points, one AppleSmartBattery temperature, and one NAND CH0 temperature. Unsupported component cards and the derived duplicate peak card were absent; unavailable battery power was omitted.

At 18:07 the rebuilt installed app separately labeled 3 source groups and 16 named measured points, and its expanded disclosure displayed PMU tdie1 through PMU tdie14, AppleSmartBattery Temperature, and NAND CH0 temp with live values. Collapsing removed all point rows and expanding restored all three families. Evidence: /tmp/mac-dashboard-qa-2026-08-29/thermal-all-named-points.jpeg.
Socket trust remains root:admin 0660 and invalid fan indexes or RPM outside measured hardware bounds fail closed. Manual fan writes were not executed.

prd_items.title: Fact-based AI project and session model
prd_items.summary: Implemented project folder to main session to subagent relationships backed by explicit provider identifiers. Every container level is independently collapsible and large branches page in bounded batches; metadata-only Recent/History records remain opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Active state comes from exact Codex turn status or matching provider process, project CWD, and recent transcript activity; otherwise the state is Idle or Inactive.
Project path is the exact cwd or an explicit user mapping; title keywords never choose a project.
Subagents require an explicit parent session identifier; otherwise they appear under Unlinked.
Provider-reported token fields remain separate from the API-equivalent standard-rate estimate; actual billed credits are not presented.
API-equivalent estimates require one exactly priced model and complete billable token buckets; unknown or ambiguous inputs fail closed, and project rollups disclose partial estimate coverage.

Records with only a real session ID/path/timestamp remain in the history index but are hidden from Recent/History usage analysis by default; enabling the activity-only filter omits nonexistent model/token/cost rows.
Today totals include only usage events that occurred today.

test_cases.expected: IDs, titles, cwd, status and token totals align.
evidence: The installed Active view showed three current Codex inProgress tasks with exact project cwd, title and cumulative token counts: mac-tool-kit #01a047b9, travian-tools #01a042a1 and hunterest #01a03d16.

At 20:27 the installed Recent view exposed explicit hierarchy counts before expansion: ai-awesome had 1 main and 166 children, artogo-infra had 1 main and 136 children, ai-driven-company had 1 main and 2 children, and backend had 0 local main records plus 23 children whose parents were absent from the local index.
Selecting Claude child #a9a64de4 displayed its provider parent #3b85a905; expanding the main row rendered the child list, and a manual refresh preserved the user's collapsed state.

The previous Unlinked Claude Runtime bucket is now presented as Claude internal background work with 12 independent runtime records because those provider files explicitly report non-sidechain records under ~/.claude rather than project subagents. Evidence: /tmp/mac-dashboard-qa-2026-08-29/ai-session-hierarchy-final.png and /tmp/mac-dashboard-qa-2026-08-29/ai-session-children-final.png.

prd_items.title: Active, recent, and history lifecycle
prd_items.summary: Implemented Active/Idle/Inactive, Recent 24h, and permanent History separation with an atomic Application Support index. Permanent History is manually refreshed, collapsed by default and batch-rendered; native History browsing is verified.
acceptance_criteria: Active means an exact Codex running state or a matching provider process and project CWD plus recent session-log activity.
Idle means the task is open but no work is executing.
Inactive tasks move to Recent immediately and to History after a configurable 24-hour default.
History is retained until the source log is deleted or the user chooses deletion; no silent parser-limit eviction.
Transcript span, active execution time, and last activity are separate fields.

use_cases: Browse and filter historical AI sessions
test_cases.fixture: Provider logs spanning reboot and multiple days
steps: Search History by project and provider
test_cases.expected: Lifecycle and retention match the declared policy without data loss.
evidence: Lifecycle boundary, permanent retention, active-state sanitization and explicit parent-link tests passed.
Recent/History metadata-only records are retained permanently but default-hidden behind an explicit activity-only toggle; Active never applies this hiding rule.

For the 6,244-record, 61-project installed History, final UI automation measured 1.490 seconds from click through accessibility capture while collapsed; Hunterest measured 1.376 seconds through the same path with 40 rows and a remaining-count load-more control. These timings include automation and capture overhead and are not pure render benchmarks.
A real new-chat main session exposed two explicit children and then fully hid both children and the child paging control when collapsed.
Project-level CWD evidence cannot label a session older than 24 hours Idle without an exact session identifier.

prd_items.title: Measured storage composition and safe reclaim workflow
prd_items.summary: Implemented a bounded, lower-bound storage composition scan, exact cleanup allow-list, impact-ranked opt-in confirmation flow, Docker-specific guidance, and responsive Process Manager columns. Temporary-fixture cleanup and the installed selection flow pass; a real-file destructive run and automated screenshot regression remain intentionally uncovered.
acceptance_criteria: Named storage categories are measured from disclosed paths; unscanned and system space remains explicitly unclassified.
Cleanup candidates expose measured size, impact, consequence, and exact management method before selection.
Cleanup rejects paths outside an exact allow-list and requires a non-empty selection plus destructive confirmation.
The cleanup sheet exposes a pointer-reachable footer Cancel action and the standard Escape shortcut without invoking cleanup.
Docker volumes and active containers are never included in ordinary file cleanup; Docker-reported reclaimable storage has separate instructions.
Cleanup reports a fresh selected-item size decrease and volume free-space delta instead of promising the pre-scan estimate.
The Process Manager toolbar and all eight tabs remain readable at the installed app minimum viewport.

test_cases.fixture: Temporary category roots plus the current Mac home and Docker read-only storage report
steps: Compare measured totals with fixture files
Cancel by pointer and by Escape
test_cases.expected: Measured totals are factual, unsafe paths fail closed, selected cleanup is confirmed, and the after-state is remeasured.
evidence: Six StorageManagementTests pass: named-path measurement, non-negative unclassified math, Docker volume separation, exact allow-list rejection, empty-selection no-op, and bounded partial scans.

The installed scan completed within the 10.76-second observation window and showed 49.5 GiB of successfully read named categories against 525.9 GiB used, with 476.3 GiB explicitly unclassified and eight partial categories; these are a live lower-bound snapshot, not a full macOS Storage index.

The installed cleanup sheet started with no selection, exposed each path, impact and consequence, and required a second destructive confirmation after selecting only npm cache. The confirmation was cancelled; no user files were deleted.

Docker-reported Images, Containers, Volumes and Build Cache remain separate. Volumes are labeled high impact and no volume-prune action is provided. Evidence: /tmp/mac-dashboard-qa-2026-08-29/final-disk-composition.png.

The title-bar-adjacent Cancel control was moved into the fixed footer with a 72-point minimum button width and the standard Escape shortcut. The installed app dismissed the sheet through a pointer click at screenshot-local coordinate (445, 492), then reopened and dismissed it with Escape; no cleanup confirmation was invoked. Evidence: /tmp/mac-dashboard-qa-2026-08-29/storage-cleanup-cancel-fixed.png.

decisions.decision: Use exact Codex turn status for Active; otherwise cross-check provider process, project CWD, and 30-second transcript freshness to classify Active, Idle, or Inactive.
Use a 24-hour Recent buffer after a task becomes inactive, then move it to History without deleting it.
Remove actual billing from the UI; when exact model and billable token buckets exist, show a dated official-rate API-equivalent estimate by default and label it as non-billing.

Only render measured physical temperature component cards. Keep provider metadata-only AI records for provenance, but hide them from Recent/History usage analysis by default and never hide real Active records.

Default permanent History to collapsed projects, page each expanded branch in 40-row batches, refresh Active every 10 seconds and Recent every 30 seconds, and refresh History only on explicit request.
Remove purge from RAM and Lag remediation because macOS purge only clears disk buffer cache and cannot clear VM inactive pages; explain inactive pages as automatically reclaimable instead.

Use measured storage inventory, impact-ranked opt-in selection, destructive confirmation, an exact cleanup allow-list, and after-state measurement. Keep Docker storage externally managed and never include volumes in ordinary cleanup.
